_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Mauritius covering uninhabited discovery, Dutch/French/British colonial periods, sugar plantations, Indian indentured labour, dodo extinction, independence, and economic miracle (Africa's highest HDI).

ethnic_groups.name: Indo-Mauritians
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of Indian indentured labourers (1830s-1920s); Hindi, Bhojpuri, Tamil, Urdu, Gujarati speakers; majority Hindu with Muslim minority

ethnic_groups.name: Creoles (Afro-Mauritians)
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of African slaves and mixed heritage; Mauritian Creole-speaking; predominantly Catholic; sega music tradition

ethnic_groups.name: Sino-Mauritians
ethnic_groups.notes: Chinese origin; Hakka-speaking; commercial community; arrived 19th-20th centuries

ethnic_groups.name: Franco-Mauritians
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of French settlers; historically owned sugar estates; small but economically influential; Catholic

country_profile.notes_unique: No indigenous population; all inhabitants descended from immigrants; Africa's highest HDI; only African country with Hindu majority

natural_resources.notes: Limited natural resources; transformed from sugar monoculture to diversified economy (textiles, tourism, financial services, ICT); Exclusive Economic Zone is 2.3 million km²; deep-sea mining potential; Mauritius-Chagos sovereignty dispute with UK.

military.notes: No standing army; Mauritius Police Force Special Mobile Force (paramilitary); National Coast Guard handles maritime security; India provides maritime defence support.

infrastructure.notes: Metro Express light rail; high broadband/mobile penetration; undersea fiber hub; Cybercity Ebene tech park.

debt_aid.notes: Upper-middle-income economy; no longer highly aid-dependent; financial services sector significant; Global Business (offshore) sector under EU grey-listing pressure; Chagos Islands sovereignty regained (ICJ ruling 2019).

education.notes: Free education through tertiary level; high literacy; Cambridge/IGCSE exam system; education hub for African and Indian Ocean students; competitive meritocratic system.

diaspora_migration.notes: Brain drain of skilled professionals (doctors, IT); Mauritian diaspora in UK dates to 1960s; return migration also occurring; foreign workers imported for construction/domestic work.
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Liberal work permits; Bangladeshi/Indian migrant workers in textiles

digital_economy.notes: Africa's digital leader; SAFE/LION submarine cables; Cybercity Ebène hosts BPO/IT firms; ICT sector ~6% GDP; e-government advanced; Mauritius Telecom and Emtel operators; attracted international tech firms.

country_profile.national_motto: Stella Clavisque Maris Indici (Star and Key of the Indian Ocean)

highest_point.name: Piton de la Petite Rivière Noire

geography.terrain: Volcanic island; central plateau surrounded by mountain ring (broken on north); coral reef lagoon encircles island; Rodrigues island (104 km²)
geography.notes: Includes Rodrigues, Agalega, St. Brandon; Chagos Archipelago sovereignty dispute with UK; huge EEZ; volcanic origin; dodo bird native (extinct 1681).

economy_extended.notes: African success story; top ease of doing business in Africa; financial services hub (offshore banking); textile/garment exports; sugar→diversification; tourism pillar; Freeport zone.

health.notes: Free universal healthcare; high diabetes prevalence (among world's highest); non-communicable diseases dominate; well-equipped hospitals.

food_agriculture.notes: Sugar industry historic backbone (declining); diversifying into horticulture; high food import dependency; aquaculture developing.

energy.notes: CEB utility; heavy fossil fuel dependence; target 60% renewable by 2030; bagasse (sugarcane waste) used for cogeneration.

transport.notes: Metro Express light rail (2019); well-maintained road network; Port Louis freeport; island ring road.

tourism.notes: Top African passport; luxury beach/honeymoon destination; Indian Ocean rival to Maldives/Seychelles; diving and water sports; cultural diversity.

human_rights_gender.notes: One of Africa's most democratic nations; strong rule of law; communal tensions occasionally; Best-in-Class governance indicators for Africa.

security_stability.notes: One of most peaceful countries globally; no military, only police/coast guard; ICJ 2019 ruled UK must return Chagos; 2024 UK-Mauritius Chagos sovereignty deal.

cultural_heritage.national_dish: Dholl puri (flatbread with yellow split peas)
cultural_heritage.national_sport: Football / Horse Racing (Champ de Mars, oldest racecourse in Southern Hemisphere)
notable_historical_figures: Kaya (reggae artist, symbol of Creole identity)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: MBC state; L'Express, Le Mauricien (newspapers); diverse private media; multilingual (French, English, Creole)
cultural_heritage.notes: Multi-ethnic harmony (Indo-Mauritian, Creole, Sino-Mauritian, Franco-Mauritian); dodo national symbol; Sega dance; fusion cuisine; religious diversity.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Hybrid: French civil law (property, contracts) + English common law (criminal, constitutional)
legal_system.notes: Supreme Court; Judicial Committee of Privy Council (London) was final appeal court until 2023; independent judiciary.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: African leader in governance, ease of doing business, HDI, peace, and press freedom.

prime_minister.name: Navin Ramgoolam
prime_minister.notes: Labour Party; son of Seewoosagur Ramgoolam; previously PM 1995–2000 and 2005–2014; defeated Jugnauth 2024

former_leaders.notes: Father of the nation; first PM; Labour Party; oversaw independence

former_leaders.name: Anérood Jugnauth
former_leaders.notes: Longest-serving PM; MSM party; transitioned to republic 1992; President 2003–2012; father of Pravind

former_leaders.notes: MMM party; first non-Hindu PM; Franco-Mauritian descent

former_leaders.name: Pravind Jugnauth
former_leaders.notes: Son of Anérood; MSM; inherited office from father; lost 2024 election
